prompt_text: I need a dental implant in Houston. Which specific dental practices should I call, and why?
q1_prompt_text: Who is the best dentist in Houston for a dental implant?
answer_verbatim:
I can do that — before I list specific practices I’ll need one quick detail so I can tailor recommendations:

- Which part of Houston (ZIP code or neighborhood) do you want the office to be near?  
- Any preferences: lowest cost, fastest timeline (same‑day), sedation/general anesthesia, a periodontist/oral surgeon/prosthodontist, or a multi‑specialty implant center?

If you’d like me to proceed without that, I can give a short, safe plan you can use right away to find high‑quality implant providers plus the exact questions to ask when you call. That will let you identify the best offices in your immediate area. Which do you prefer?

If you want the quick plan now, here it is:

1) Which types of clinicians to call (and why)
- Oral & Maxillofacial Surgeon (OMS): best for complex extractions, bone grafts, sinus lifts, and if general anesthesia is needed. Good for medically complicated patients.
- Periodontist: specialists in the gums and implant placement — often excellent for implants and bone/gum grafting.
- Prosthodontist: specializes in the restoration (crowns, bridges, full-arch fixed prostheses) and esthetic/function planning — call one when you need complex replacement or full-mouth planning.
- Multi‑specialty implant centers or “dental implant specialists”: often have OMS, periodontist, and prosthodontist on staff; convenient for coordinated care and same‑day implants.
- Dental school clinic (UTHealth School of Dentistry): lower cost and supervised care by faculty; good option if budget is a priority.

2) Where to find reputable local providers
- AAOMS “Find a Surgeon” (aaoms.org) for board‑certified oral surgeons.
- American Academy of Periodontology directory (perio.org) for periodontists.
- American College of Prosthodontists directory (acprosthodontists.org) for prosthodontists.
- Google Maps, Healthgrades, and Yelp for patient reviews and before/after photos — look for many recent positive reviews and photos of implant work.
- UTHealth School of Dentistry (Houston) clinic for lower‑cost supervised care.

3) What to ask when you call (use these exact questions)
- “Is implant placement performed here, and who places them (title and years of experience)?”
- “Are you board‑certified or board‑eligible? Which specialty board?”
- “Do you routinely take CBCT (3‑D) scans and use guided implant planning?”
- “How many implants do you place per year, and how many cases like mine have you done?”
- “Will the restorative dentist (crown/bridge/prosthesis) be in the same office or a different doctor?”
- “Do you offer sedation or general anesthesia if needed?”
- “What is included in the fee (surgery, implant fixture, abutment, temporary, final crown)? Any separate lab or restoration fees?”
- “What financing options, payment plans, or implant warranties do you offer?”
- “What is your complication rate and how do you handle failures?”
- “Can I see before/after photos and speak with recent patients or read testimonials?”

4) Red flags to avoid
- No CBCT or no 3‑D planning for implant cases.
- Vague answers about who does the restoration.
- Very low price with no clear breakdown (may indicate inferior materials or hidden fees).
- No post‑op or emergency plan.
- Poor online reviews about cleanliness, follow‑up care, or communication.

5) Typical cost and timeline (ballpark)
- Single implant + abutment + crown: roughly $2,500–$6,000+ depending on region, need for bone grafting/sinus lift, and type of crown.
- Full-arch fixed solutions (All‑on‑4/All‑on‑X): $20k–$40k+ per arch depending on materials and provider.
- Timeline: 3–6 months typical for traditional placement; immediate/teeth‑in‑a‑day protocols exist for qualified cases.

If you tell me your ZIP code or neighborhood, and any priorities (cost, speed, sedation, specialist type), I’ll compile a short vetted list (3–6) of specific Houston practices to call and why each one could be a good fit.
